table_title: List the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction winners 2000-2024 inclusive whose per-author Wikipedia article explicitly grounds an Author Birth State or Country (24 rows after 1 per-row exclusion of Paul Harding 2010 whose article does not explicitly state a birth state); 2012 was not awarded; 2023 was shared by two co-winners; Colson Whitehead won twice within the window. The Author Birth State or Country cell is heterogeneous: U.S. state or Washington, D.C. for U.S.-born authors; modern sovereign country for the 5 foreign-born winners.
db_analog: SELECT year, author, book, author_birth_state_or_country FROM pulitzer_fiction_winners_with_author_birth WHERE year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2024 AND year != 2012 AND per_author_article_grounds_birth_state_or_country = TRUE ORDER BY year, author
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'Pulitzer Prize for Fiction' master article (winners table) + 24 per-author Wikipedia articles, accessed 2026-05-15. Universe is the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction winners 2000-2024 inclusive whose per-author Wikipedia article explicitly grounds a birth state or country — a hard 25-year temporal window on the source-defined winners-table membership, with 2012 excluded as a no-award year (judges deadlocked), 2023 contributing 2 rows for the co-winners (Barbara Kingsolver + Hernan Diaz shared the prize that year), and 1 per-row exclusion for the 2010 winner Paul Harding (Tinkers) whose Wikipedia article does not explicitly state a birth state (only that he 'grew up in Wenham, Massachusetts', which under the strict Born-field rule is raised-not-born and therefore not source-grounded as a birth-state cell). Row count = 24 rows = 24 award years (2000-2024 minus 2012 no-award) + 1 extra row for the 2023 co-winner - 1 row excluded for Paul Harding 2010. Post-window exclusions: 2025 Percival Everett / 'James' and 2026 Daniel Kraus / 'Angel Down' are both outside the staged 2000-2024 window per current Pulitzer table state; pre-2000 winners (Michael Cunningham 1999 The Hours, Philip Roth 1998 American Pastoral, etc.) are also explicitly excluded. Per-row cells: Year is integer year of the award per the master winners table; Author is the winning author's name verbatim from the master winners table (composite PK part 2 with Year as PK part 1); Book is the winning book title verbatim from the master winners table; Author Birth State or Country is heterogeneous-typed per the documented normalization rule — for U.S.-born authors, the U.S. state or 'Washington, D.C.' (federal district) from the per-author article's 'Born' field; for the 5 foreign-born authors (Jhumpa Lahiri UK, Geraldine Brooks Australia, Junot Díaz Dominican Republic, Viet Thanh Nguyen Vietnam, Hernan Diaz Argentina), the modern sovereign country containing the birthplace, with constituent-country normalization (e.g., Lahiri born London, England → United Kingdom per the Booker-instance precedent). Citizenship, nationality, residence, and raised-in location are NOT used. Colson Whitehead won twice within the window (2017 The Underground Railroad, 2020 The Nickel Boys); composite PK (Year, Author) handles this as 2 rows. The 24-row universe is stable on a multi-year horizon: the Pulitzer Fiction winners are well-documented and won't change retroactively.
_extraction_notes: Original instance chipping `implicit_join` from gap 2 to **gap 1** (6 of 8 staged before this; this brings the count to 7 of 8). Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, source_count = 24 — 1 master 'Pulitzer Prize for Fiction' Wikipedia article (winners table) + 23 per-author Wikipedia articles (23 distinct authors after the cycle-1 Paul Harding row exclusion; Colson Whitehead won twice but has 1 article). The pre-staging audit design review (1 round) selected Variant A (heterogeneous Author Birth State or Country cell) over Variant B (US-born only, 20 rows) and Variant C (Birth Country only, mirrors Booker but low variance). Variant A preserves the full source-defined Pulitzer universe (5 foreign-born winners retained) while preserving state-level granularity for U.S.-born winners. Audit recommended 4 pre-staging fixes all applied in cycle-0: (1) renamed cell from 'Author Birthplace' to 'Author Birth State or Country' (makes mixed granularity honest; 'Birthplace' wrongly suggests city-level values); (2) Lahiri cell = 'United Kingdom' per the Booker-instance modern-sovereign-country normalization rule, NOT 'England' (constituent country); (3) Washington, D.C. is used as its own value for Chabon and Greer (federal-district source-verbatim, not coerced to a state or 'District of Columbia' formal name); (4) Hernan Diaz URL is Hernan_Diaz_(writer) NOT the disambiguation page Hernan_Diaz which redirects to a footballer. Pipeline: (1) fetch the cited Pulitzer Prize for Fiction Wikipedia article HTML and extract the winners-table rows for 2000-2024 inclusive (skipping 2012 no-award); (2) for each row, take Year + Author + Book verbatim from the winners table; (3) for each of 23 distinct authors (24 minus Paul Harding excluded in cycle-1), fetch the per-author Wikipedia article and extract the 'Born' field's normalized value (U.S. state for U.S.-born; modern sovereign country for foreign-born). Result: 24 rows × 4 columns, composite PK (Year, Author), 0 duplicates. Author Birth State or Country distribution (19 distinct values across 14 distinct U.S. states/DC + 5 foreign countries): U.S. = New York 3 (Russo, Whitehead x2), Washington D.C. 3 (Chabon, Greer, Edward P. Jones), Illinois 2 (Egan, Powers), Michigan 1 (Eugenides), Idaho 1 (Marilynne Robinson), Rhode Island 1 (McCarthy), Maine 1 (Strout), South Dakota 1 (Adam Johnson), Mississippi 1 (Tartt), Ohio 1 (Doerr), Minnesota 1 (Erdrich), New Jersey 1 (Cohen), Maryland 1 (Kingsolver), West Virginia 1 (Phillips) = 14 U.S. states/DC × 19 rows; foreign = United Kingdom 1 (Lahiri), Australia 1 (Brooks), Dominican Republic 1 (Junot Díaz), Vietnam 1 (Nguyen), Argentina 1 (Hernan Diaz) = 5 countries × 5 rows. Confidence gradient: very-LLM-knowable cells include canonical Pulitzer winners (Lahiri 2000, McCarthy 2007 The Road, Tartt 2014 The Goldfinch, Doerr 2015 All the Light We Cannot See, Whitehead 2017 + 2020); mid-difficulty cells include the well-known but less-headline-grabbing winners (Eugenides 2003, Russo 2002, Robinson 2005, Strout 2009, Egan 2011); harder calibration cells include the recent/less-known winners (Cohen 2022, Kingsolver 2023, Hernan Diaz 2023, Phillips 2024) and the foreign-born exceptions where the cell value is a country rather than a state. Implicit-join structure: master Pulitzer article gives (Year, Author, Book) as a denormalized winners table; per-author Wikipedia articles supply Author Birth State or Country — a clean single-master-multiple-per-entity implicit join matching the precedent set by the parallel-Booker booker_prize_for_fiction_winners_2000_2024 instance (which uses the cleaner all-country Author Birth Country cell for the UK-Commonwealth-and-Ireland universe). The Pulitzer instance's heterogeneous cell is acceptable per audit Variant-A approval because the column name 'Author Birth State or Country' makes the heterogeneity honest.
